items.title: TheGentlemen claims MegChem (South Africa)
items.summary: On 2 November 2026 TheGentlemen ransomware group listed MegChem, a South African engineering consultancy, on its leak site; the victim has not publicly confirmed.

items.title: Queens Public Library — ransomware outage across 66 branches
items.summary: Ransomware knocked out computers, Wi-Fi, self-checkout and the website at all 66 Queens Public Library branches; the library confirmed ransomware but no group has claimed it (publication date not independently verified).

items.title: n0n group claims Finzly Corp (late-October carryover)
items.summary: Payments-platform vendor Finzly was listed by the n0n group with a 19 October 2026 date, which raises third-party exposure for the banks that use it.

items.title: Vicksburg, MS — city systems still recovering (October carryover)
items.summary: A 1 October 2026 ransomware attack forced the city of Vicksburg, Mississippi, to take several computer systems offline and disrupted municipal operations.

ransomware.note: Few confirmed November victims were indexed yet; two October carryovers are included for context. BlackFog's November roundup is expected in early December.

items.title: GitHub — Actions and pull-request failures
items.summary: On 5 November more than 570 Downdetector reports cited 502 errors and failed pull requests and Actions runs; trackers logged it as a minor incident, resolved the same night.

items.title: Instagram — login and feed issues
items.summary: About 200 users reported login, feed and messaging problems on 7 November; it was limited in scope, with no platform-wide outage confirmed.

items.title: Brightspeed ISP outage — NC, OH, PA
items.summary: Outage maps logged a regional Brightspeed internet outage on 3 November with about 919 user reports across North Carolina, Ohio and Pennsylvania.

outage.note: No major AWS, Azure or GCP outage found for November so far. The most recent hyperscaler event was Azure's two outages, 29 Sep–1 Oct, across 18 regions.

items.title: CISA KEV: WordPress core TOCTOU race condition (CVE-2026-119977)
items.summary: CISA added the actively exploited WordPress core race-condition flaw (CVSS 8.1) to the KEV catalog on 3 November 2026.

items.title: CISA KEV: CVE-2026-19868 added 6 Nov, federal due date 20 Nov
items.summary: The KEV catalog lists CVE-2026-19868 as added 6 November with a 20 November remediation deadline for federal agencies; check the catalog for the affected product.

items.title: Four new KEV entries in the past 7 days
items.summary: Senserva's tracker counts 4 CVEs added to CISA KEV in the week to 6 November 2026, a steady exploited-vulnerability cadence for patch prioritisation.

items.title: WordPress core flaw draws active exploitation warning
items.summary: Hackread reports attackers are exploiting the WordPress core TOCTOU bug, found by a Picus Security researcher, putting a very large install base at risk until it is patched.

items.title: OpenAM session-token theft and SAML bypass (CVE-2026-123551)
items.summary: Researchers disclosed OpenAM flaws that allow session-token theft and SAML authentication bypass; they were not in KEV as of 8 November.

items.title: Catastrophic flooding — North Georgia and southern Tennessee
items.summary: Flash flood emergencies brought water rescues and evacuations; the river crested above its 1990 record at McCaysville and Copperhill.

items.title: B.C. atmospheric-river storm — Vancouver Island emergency
items.summary: Zeballos declared a local state of emergency and evacuated 22 properties over landslide risk on 6 November; more than 400 mm of rain is possible and thousands of BC Hydro customers lost power.

items.title: Los Angeles County — strong winds and elevated fire risk
items.summary: On 6 November LA County officials urged residents to prepare for strong winds and elevated fire-weather risk and to check evacuation zones.

physical.note: USGS significant-earthquake feed: no significant quakes this week.
